quickSummary: Bent's Rule states more electronegative substituents prefer hybrid orbitals with lower s-character (axial pd in TBP), while lone pairs and multiple bonds prefer higher s-character (equatorial sp²).

summaryBox.title: Bent's Rule
summaryBox.takeaway: More electronegative atoms prefer less s-character (axial pd). Lone pairs and double bonds prefer more s-character (equatorial sp²).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
BENT'S RULE IN TBP GEOMETRY (sp³d)
                         
   Equatorial Positions (sp² hybrid): 33.3% s-character ──► Binds Lone Pairs & Double Bonds
   Axial Positions      (pd hybrid):   0% s-character   ──► Binds Electronegative atoms (F, Cl)
conceptBreakdown.content:
In Trigonal Bipyramidal ($sp^3d$) geometry:
• **Equatorial orbitals ($sp^2$)**: $33.3\%\ s$-character. Lower energy, hold electron density close $\rightarrow$ host lone pairs and electropositive groups.
• **Axial orbitals ($pd = p_z + d_{z^2}$)**: $0\%\ s$-character. Elongated lobes $\rightarrow$ host highly electronegative atoms ($\text{F, Cl}$).

conceptBreakdown.title: 6.2 PCl3F2 Isomerism & Participating d-Orbitals
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PCl₃F₂ GEOMETRIC ISOMERISM
                        
           Axial Fluorines (0% s-character)
                 F
                 │
      Cl ─────── P ─────── Cl   (Equatorial Chlorines: 33.3% s-character)
                 │
                 F
           Axial Fluorines
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Participating Atomic Orbitals**:
- **$dsp^2$**: $\mathbf{d_{x^2-y^2}} + s + p_x + p_y$ (Square Planar, e.g. $[\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}$)
- **$sp^3d$**: $s + p_x + p_y + p_z + \mathbf{d_{z^2}}$ (Trigonal Bipyramidal, e.g. $\text{PCl}_5$)
- **$sp^3d^2$**: $s + p_x + p_y + p_z + \mathbf{d_{x^2-y^2} + d_{z^2}}$ (Octahedral, e.g. $\text{SF}_6$)
- **$sp^3d^3$**: $s + p_x + p_y + p_z + \mathbf{d_{x^2-y^2} + d_{z^2} + d_{xy}}$ (Pentagonal Bipyramidal, e.g. $\text{IF}_7$)

quickRevision: Bent's Rule: Electronegative atoms in axial (pd), lone pairs in equatorial (sp²).
In PCl₃F₂, both Fluorine atoms occupy axial positions.
dsp² uses d_x²-y²; sp³d uses d_z²; sp³d² uses d_x²-y² + d_z².
In PCl₅, axial bonds (2.14 Å) are longer and weaker than equatorial bonds (2.02 Å).
